issues.legal_issue: A party may not object to relief under the law of restitution for lack of a necessary pleading after both parties have invited the court to determine that relief and supplied material for it.
material_facts: After tentatively finding the agreement void, the High Court invited both parties to provide material for determining compensation under the law of restitution.
Both parties supplied affidavits and other material and asked the High Court to determine the issue so that it could pass an appropriate decree.
issues.conclusion: The objection that the State had not pleaded for an adjustment under the law of restitution could not be raised in the appeals.
issues.legal_principle: Where parties, without demur, invite a court to decide an issue and provide material for that decision, they cannot later object that the relief was unavailable for want of a necessary plea.

predicates.appeal_from_restitution_decree: The proceeding is an appeal from a decree determining relief arising from a void agreement.
predicates.parties_invited_determination: Both parties asked the court to determine the restitutionary issue.
predicates.parties_supplied_supporting_material: Both parties provided affidavits or other material for deciding that issue.

issues.definition: When an appeal from a restitution decree follows the parties' joint invitation to decide the issue and their submission of supporting material, an objection based on the absence of a pleading is unavailable.

issues.legal_issue: Compensation for benefits received under a void mineral-extraction agreement is measured by reasonable royalty and compensation for any exclusive privilege, rather than by the recipient's profits from all its businesses.
material_facts: The agreement granting quarrying rights was held void, and the parties did not dispute that finding.
The company's reported net profits covered several businesses, including quarrying, polishing, flooring work, and dealing in building materials; it kept no separate accounts for those activities.
The State had granted the company exclusive quarrying rights over a large area.
The High Court used reasonable royalty for extracted stone and separately assessed compensation for the exclusive rights.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was right to use reasonable royalty as the measure for the extracted stone and to award additional compensation for the exclusive privilege; the company's profits from all its activities were not the proper measure.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 65 of the Contract Act, restoration or compensation for advantages received under a void agreement is mutual. Firm Govindram Seksaria v. Edward Radbone was relied on for the principle that each party must restore advantages received from the other. Because the State could recover the value of the rough stone but would have to account for the company's extraction expenses, reasonable royalty was an appropriate measure; compensation was also due for the exclusive rights granted. Net profits combining unrelated business activities were not an appropriate measure.

rule.if: restitution_under_void_agreement and mineral_extraction_arrangement and profits_combine_unrelated_businesses and exclusive_extraction_rights_granted

predicates.restitution_under_void_agreement: The proceeding concerns restoration or compensation for benefits received under an agreement found void.
predicates.mineral_extraction_arrangement: The void agreement granted rights to extract minerals or stone in return for payment.
predicates.profits_combine_unrelated_businesses: The recipient's reported profits include activities beyond extracting and selling the mineral or stone, without separate accounts for those activities.
predicates.exclusive_extraction_rights_granted: The grantor gave the recipient exclusive extraction rights over an area.

issues.definition: If a void mineral-extraction arrangement produced combined profits from unrelated businesses and granted exclusive extraction rights, compensation is based on reasonable royalty and the value of those rights.

issues.legal_issue: A court deciding restitution for the period after a suit was filed may determine and deduct the compensation due for that period rather than order an unconditional refund that necessitates further litigation.
material_facts: The company paid the State amounts during the period after filing its suit.
The High Court ordered the entire amount paid for that period to be refunded because it considered itself unable to determine compensation for the period.
The Supreme Court determined reasonable royalty and compensation for the exclusive privilege for that period and deducted those amounts from the payments before fixing the refund.
issues.conclusion: The High Court's direction to refund all payments for the later period without adjustment was unjustified; the refund had to be reduced by the compensation due to the State.
issues.legal_principle: In applying Section 65 of the Contract Act, a court may account for the mutual restitution due for the period in dispute. An unconditional refund that leaves compensation to be pursued in separate litigation serves no purpose other than multiplying proceedings. In the circumstances, the Court assessed compensation using reasonable royalty and a separate amount for the exclusive privilege.

predicates.appeal_from_restitution_decree: The proceeding is an appeal from a decree determining restitution under a void agreement.
predicates.payments_made_for_later_period: The recipient made payments to the grantor for the period being considered after the restitution claim was filed.
predicates.compensation_due_for_that_period: The grantor is entitled to compensation for extraction or exclusive rights during that period.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns payments for a later period and compensation is due for that period, the refund is reduced by the compensation due.

issues.legal_issue: A restitutionary adjustment is barred for amounts that became payable outside the applicable limitation period before the suit was filed.
material_facts: The suit was filed after the amounts relating to two earlier accounting years had become payable.
Those amounts had become payable before the period for which the High Court allowed an adjustment.
issues.conclusion: The High Court correctly disallowed an adjustment for the two earlier years on the ground of limitation.
issues.legal_principle: A claim for adjustment cannot be allowed when it is barred by limitation; the Court accepted the High Court's conclusion because the relevant amounts had become payable before the suit was filed by the time relevant to the limitation ruling.

predicates.restitution_adjustment_claim: A party seeks an adjustment for amounts connected with a restitutionary claim.
predicates.claim_accrued_outside_limitation_period: The amounts sought to be adjusted became payable so long before the suit that the claim was outside the applicable limitation period.

issues.definition: A restitutionary adjustment claim is time-barred when the amounts it concerns became payable outside the applicable limitation period.
